approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent SMILES prior from unlabeled molecules and chooses its checkpoint by the yield of valid, connected, distinct ancestral samples, with heldout likelihood breaking ties. Each objective receives a fresh adaptable copy and a frozen reference. Accepted molecular trajectories train the adaptable policy through trajectory balance, a learned normalizer and prior regularization. The online cycle emits one neural batch followed by two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh the scored breeding population and supply a protected first graph descendant. The graph operator independently cuts the two selected parents, usually retains the larger first fragment and smaller second fragment, and joins their exposed atoms with a single bond. Atom and bond mutations may follow. An accepted-score fingerprint posterior chooses the remaining evaluations from a temporary offspring pool, and accepted graph descendants return to neural replay. The join currently requires molecular validity but does not check whether either attachment resembles the bond environment it replaces.
approach.novelty: Add reciprocal cut-endpoint context matching to crossover: a retained endpoint may replace the opposite parent's discarded endpoint only when their local typed neighborhoods agree. This makes the actual attachment sites, rather than whole-molecule resemblance or complete-ring retention, the unit of compatibility. The lineage's previous siblings changed prior preparation or accepted-score neural behavior; related campaign experiments favored similar parents or preserved complete ring cores while leaving attachment compatibility unresolved. This experiment changes only the admissibility of the already sampled two-cut graft. A mismatch returns to the Parent's existing mutation path, and crossover involving its whole-fragment hydrogen-attachment fallback remains explicitly outside the gate.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 completes all supplied replicas with macro mean 0.5501977216134929 and population SD 0.02173839408580094; its paired changes against its own Parent are +0.02628512092174895, +0.05155306437585694 and +0.010747210357020975. The actual per-seed summaries and run logs confirm complete valid batches, so this is a chemical allocation question rather than an observed batch-completion failure. Its graph logs contain 20,638 crossover attempts and 20,630 successful sanitized crossovers among 45,342 graph-generation attempts. Only 121 of 1,133 evaluated crossover descendants beat their best generating parent; the pure-crossover subset has 62 beats among 604 evaluations. These descriptive rates do not prove crossover causes the endpoint deficit. A direct trace does expose the missing local constraint: a pure self-crossover joins an oxygen-bearing fragment to an aryl nitrogen fragment, introducing an O-N connection into a parent that had ordinary methoxy and amide relationships; the accepted score falls from 0.3051048083696145 to 0.034034649500005586. The molecular assessment independently identifies context-breaking polar-group changes alongside useful rings. Related node n-a20706504e8f confirms that more similar whole parents can still produce incompatible physical attachments and lower final scores. Node n-822f049d9c70 preserves complete first-parent ring cores but increases emitted size and loses score, while n-9bee44b1c9c3 preserves C=O endpoints but still changes their neighboring functional-group classes. The behavior targeted here is accepting a cross-parent single-bond join without comparing the local environments on the two sides of each cut; neither ring preservation nor parser validity establishes that correspondence.
hypothesis: Gate two-cut graph crossover by reciprocal equality of the retained and opposite discarded endpoint contexts, preserving the Parent fragment draws and routing mismatches through its existing mutation fallback.

finding_summary.headline: Attachment matching worked, but crossover nearly vanished and one replica failed
finding_summary.insights: Exact local attachment matching can suppress genuinely available mismatched grafts while preserving a small usable crossover channel. Its dominant effect here was to replace crossover with first-parent mutation: 23 of the 27 later-mutated crossover emissions had reproduced a parent before mutation, and only six evaluated emissions had a changed immediate recombination product. Better overall graph yield therefore does not establish better recombination. Mutation work rose from about 149 to 192 attempts per graph request, and scaffold variety within individual task/seed pools narrowed even though every pool filled. The rule also preserves unusual chemistry already accepted in a source: both pure crossover emissions retained N–F bonds, and the broader output still contained N–O and N–N environments and unspecified stereochemistry. The strong sitagliptin score increase cannot be read as improved synthetic quality. The completion failure is separately explained by an inherited molecule reader alternating between two aromatic SMILES representations after a protected ring-closing mutation; it does not erase the measured gate activation. Full three-seed utility and a useful contribution from compatible recombination remain unresolved.
finding_summary.results: The gate rejected 18,963 otherwise valid joins, including 18,158 that were also novel and encodable. Every one of the 847 surviving applicable joins satisfied both independently reconstructed endpoint matches. The channel remained usable, but barely: only two changed pure crossovers reached evaluation, alongside 27 crossovers followed by mutation. Crossover evaluations fell from 1,133 to 29, and their best-parent beats fell from 121 to two. Overall graph yield improved from 452/2,850 to 541/2,710 best-parent beats; on the same observed batch prefixes, the Parent had 437/2,710. All 271 reached graph batches were full, and all 143 reserved first descendants had real current policy ancestry. However, a feedback identity error stopped one task at 90 of 300 evaluations, so the panel used 4,290 of 4,500 calls and has no complete three-seed score. The two completed seed macro scores rose from 0.542383 to 0.565620 and from 0.579854 to 0.586448. Across complete three-seed task endpoints, sitagliptin rose by 0.163068 and deco_hop by 0.010448, while median_2 fell by 0.020074 and drd2 by 0.002229. Zaleplon fell by 0.006004 over the two completed seeds.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich ureas, azaarenes and cyclic amines coexist with unusual N–O, N–N and N–F chemistry and unspecified stereochemistry.
molecular.overall_character: The supplied output of n-7ba291681388 spans recognizable medicinal scaffolds and chemically questionable derivatives. Aromatic and saturated heterocycles are abundant; ring supply is not the missing capability. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9851 to 0.9977 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.8379 to 0.9818. These are fractions of SMILES containing the respective notation, not ring counts or fractions of aromatic atoms. Every task has a stereocentre-notation rate of 0.0. Overall exploration includes several scaffold families, but the highest-scoring excerpts mostly contain close relatives within seed-specific families. Compared with parent n-dd7b8aa31113, the observed chemistry changes substantially without eliminating unusual heteroatom connections: compact ureas replace some exotic fused aromatic derivatives, smaller azaaryl assemblies retain N–O chemistry, and other trajectories concentrate on nitrogen chains or covalent N–F bonds. No synthesis, stability, protonation or biological mechanism is established by these scores. All listed tasks have trajectories. The supplied zaleplon_mpo seed-2 trajectory ends at evaluation 90, with 80 optimizer proposals; its digest contains 660 optimizer proposals across seeds. The other supplied task/seed trajectories reach evaluation 300, giving 870 optimizer proposals per task. That first comparison therefore describes the supplied prefix, not an equally complete endpoint.

per_task.generated_character: The leading family consists of moderately sized N-benzyl/N-aryl ureas with hydroxylated phenyl or pyridyl groups and aryl halogens. These have familiar carbonyl and aromatic substitution chemistry and look more straightforward to synthesize than many surrounding proposals. The other prominent digest family combines a biphenyl nitrile with an ether-linked unsaturated imine/thioamide appendage. Low-scoring proposals include very large polyaromatic structures, extended polyenes, highly decorated amides and a polysulfide linker. Rings and aromatics are pervasive, with digest rates of 0.9924 and 0.9818; mean SMILES length is 46.4, a text-length measure rather than a molecular-size descriptor.
liabilities: The imine/thioamide side chains and long unsaturated tails introduce stability and geometric-isomer questions that the recorded scores do not resolve.
Polysulfide and unusually connected nitrogen-containing alternatives require separate chemical scrutiny; the makeability of the urea family does not generalize to the entire output.
The large low-scoring polyaromatic derivatives combine substantial size with complex substitution, increasing apparent synthetic burden.
missing_features: Consistent preservation of the moderate aromatic size and restrained polar substitution seen in the leading ureas is missing from the oversized low-scoring proposals.

Distinct compact scaffolds that reproduce the leading polar-group arrangement through ordinary functional groups are weakly represented among the digest leaders. No particular absent target ring can be inferred from this sample.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The hydroxypyridyl urea scores 0.48211544265448975, versus 0.3051048083696145 for the initial trimethoxyindole amide. Replacing its aryl chlorine with bromine retains the same recorded score, while adding another phenolic hydroxyl gives 0.4588223100704468. The much larger polyene/amide structure scores 2.6967182149798692e-39. This supports a bounded aromatic framework with a particular polar-group arrangement, not unlimited aromatic or heteroatom addition. The imine/thioamide alternative still reaches 0.4711064141789182, so conventional urea chemistry is not uniquely rewarded. The parent seed-0 best was a more unusual fused aromatic N–O/sulfur-containing structure at 0.49151859442707624; the current urea family is chemically more conventional without a higher observed seed-0 maximum.

per_task.generated_character: The best excerpt is a closely related family of alkoxy-substituted quinazolines connected to fluorinated azaaryl groups through tertiary nitrogen linkers. Every listed leader retains an N–O bond; several contain an electron-rich amino-substituted alkyne, hydroxymethylated nitrogen or an oxime ether. The final seed-2 excerpt instead contains densely fused nitrogen heterocycles and chloromethyl/bromomethyl substituents. Worst examples include nonaromatic, carbonyl-rich bicyclic or peptide-like structures and a smaller fused aromatic sulfone. Familiar heteroaromatic cores give these compounds medicinal-chemistry character, but their peripheral bond chemistry makes synthetic plausibility uneven. Ring-closure and aromatic-presence rates are 0.9977 and 0.9782.
liabilities: N–O attachments, amino-substituted alkynes and N-hydroxymethyl groups warrant stability and synthetic-route scrutiny even when they receive high scores.
Some final heteroaryl derivatives carry potentially reactive chloromethyl or bromomethyl groups, and their dense fused-ring topology increases synthetic complexity.
The scores provide no evidence that replacing these questionable connections with more conventional ones would automatically improve the objective.
missing_features: Equally successful alternative azaaryl arrangements joined entirely through conventional functional-group environments are not demonstrated in the bounded best set; it is dominated by one N–O-containing architecture.

The lower-scoring ring systems lack the leading combination and placement of heteroaromatic nitrogen and peripheral N/O groups. These observations do not identify a uniquely required absent heterocycle.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The amino-alkyne-linked quinazoline reaches 0.8552185580114399; an ethylene-linked, hydroxymethylated analogue reaches 0.8437682003494467. The nonaromatic bicyclic sulfone/lactam gives 0.2596515290053845, while the small aromatic fused sulfone gives 0.26031991744066046. Thus the specific azaaryl and surrounding N/O arrangement matters more than ring presence alone; the comparison does not establish that the unusual alkyne itself is necessary. The parent seed-1 maximum of 0.8301591128254581 used a larger linked quinazoline assembly with problematic sulfur/nitrogen substituents. The current leaders retain the azaaryl pattern in a smaller assembly while still using unconventional connections.

per_task.generated_character: The highest-scoring excerpt contains moderately sized diaryl compounds bearing saturated diaza rings and an aryl-ethyl-pyrrolidine substituent. Methoxy, phenolic and aryl-halogen substitutions surround accessible aliphatic amine centres. Both aromatic surface and saturated ring volume are substantial. Other seeds explore fused aryl amines and furan-containing cyclic amines with fluorinated unsaturated substituents. Much of the main polyamine family looks synthetically interpretable, although some bridged, aminal-like or highly fluorinated variants are less straightforward. The digest ring-closure rate is 0.9897 and aromatic-presence rate is 0.9759. The charged-notation rate of 0.0069 does not mean that the numerous neutral-written amines cannot protonate.
liabilities: Substituted saturated rings contain unassigned stereogenic centres, so the reported SMILES do not identify individual stereoisomers.
Several amine centres combined with sizeable aromatic surface raise protonation and solubility questions that the score does not measure here.

The final seed-2 family includes an N-hydroxylated enamine and a hydroxy-substituted alkyne alongside fluorinated enol ethers; these peripheral groups are less conventional than the leading polyamine core.
missing_features: No missing score-driving aromatic or basic-amine feature is supported for the near-ceiling leaders; both are already present.
Stereochemically specified versions of the substituted diazacycles and bridged variants are absent from the supplied notation. The benefit of specifying them cannot be inferred from these scores.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The aryl-substituted diazacycle/pyrrolidine leader scores 0.9999999270196399. Low-scoring examples include an acylated sulfonamide at 3.8021829379963674e-05 and a hydrazone/amide at 4.1105044111594925e-05. The visible separation is aromatic hydrophobic structure combined with accessible aliphatic amines, compared with structures whose nitrogen is mostly acylated, sulfonylated or unsaturated. This is a molecular association, not evidence for a particular binding pose. Parent leaders also contain cyclic basic amines and aryl groups, including a seed-2 arylpiperazine derivative at 0.9999999657062248. The current topology changes within an already successful chemical theme.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring molecules range from moderately sized, densely fused/bridged nitrogen heterocycles to large assemblies of benzofused cyclic ureas, acylated diazacycles and branched amides. Aryl and benzodioxole groups recur. One leading family incorporates a carbonyl-adjacent chain of consecutive nonaromatic nitrogen atoms inside a complex ring system. The alternative family uses more recognizable amide bonds but accumulates substantial size and multiple stereogenic centres. Low-scoring products include an allyl azide, a nitroso dithiocarbamate and an acyclic polyene aldehyde. The ring-closure rate is 0.9943, aromatic-presence rate 0.9736 and mean SMILES length 55.5. This output has abundant ring topology, with questionable makeability in some of its most elaborate structures.
liabilities: Consecutive nonaromatic N–N bonds within heavily bridged carbonyl heterocycles create synthesis and stability questions beyond ordinary aromatic nitrogen chemistry.
The larger alternative structures combine many carbonyl groups, flexible connections and undefined stereochemistry, increasing apparent synthesis and characterization burden.
The low-scoring azide, nitroso-containing fragment and extended polyene aldehyde add reactive chemistry without reproducing the leading multiring architecture.
missing_features: Compact, coherent alternatives that combine the recurring aromatic, carbonyl and oxygenated-ring features are weakly represented among the current leaders; those features are often packaged in dense nitrogen-rich ring systems or bulky repeated amide units.

The parent leader shows a higher-scoring lactam/sulfonamide arrangement that is not reproduced among the current digest leaders. The evidence does not isolate any single absent functional group as the explanation.
Stereochemical definition is absent despite substituted ring junctions and branched saturated linkers.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fused nitrogen-chain/carbonyl leader scores 0.22513440568509824 and the large amide/cyclic-urea assembly scores 0.22341646706057433. The allyl azide scores 0.0 and the nitroso dithiocarbamate 0.018771276394456953. The gradient favors a multiring aromatic framework with carbonyl-linked nitrogen and oxygenated aryl features over small or acyclic fragments. Yet the parent seed-1 best, a benzofused lactam bearing an aryl sulfonamide/piperazine and benzodioxole arrangement, reached 0.26493557493264663. More elaborate ring fusion and nitrogen accumulation in the current leaders therefore do not establish a better arrangement of the favorable features.

per_task.generated_character: The main high-scoring family is a moderately sized, branched conjugated polyene connecting an N-fluorinated tetrazole to a tertiary sulfonamide with a fluorinated saturated sulfur ring. Another family combines azaaryl groups with a bridged cyclic sulfonamide containing an N–N–F connection. These are highly distinctive fluorine/nitrogen/sulfur-rich structures, with much less conventional medicinal chemistry than their scores alone suggest. Large polyhydroxylated or polyaromatic assemblies occupy the low end. Ring-closure and aromatic-presence rates are 0.9851 and 0.8379. The cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.092; the leading polyene has alternating conjugated double bonds, so this counter should not be mistaken for its bond pattern.
liabilities: N-fluorinated tetrazoles and N–N–F cyclic structures are unusual, potentially reactive motifs; neither isolability nor stability follows from valid SMILES or high scores.
Conjugated unsaturated chains have unspecified geometric isomerism, while other supplied trajectories contain cumulene-rich rings that require separate chemical scrutiny.
Nearby proposals introduce N–O or S–O connections and highly substituted saturated rings, compounding bond-stability and stereochemical uncertainty.
missing_features: A comparably scoring family that achieves the favored compact composition with conventional carbon-bound fluorine and stable heteroatom connectivity is not demonstrated among the leaders; the observed maxima instead retain covalent N–F bonds.

Controlled fluorine and oxygen placement is missing from many nearby proposals, whose scores fall sharply despite retaining most of the leading skeleton. No particular absent target pharmacophore is identifiable from these comparisons.
The multiply substituted sulfur rings and bridged nitrogen systems lack stereochemical specification.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The fluorinated tetrazole/polyene/sulfonamide reaches 0.6427992966407532. Adding a hydroxyl to its sulfur ring gives 0.016456246333778363; replacing a ring fluorine with bromine gives 0.228194394686288; changing its sulfonamide-to-ring methylene connection to oxygen gives 0.2710947934504371. Those near-neighbour contrasts show sensitivity to the particular F/O substitution and connectivity within this family. A large polyhydroxylated structure scores 0.0. The parent seed-2 maximum was a smaller fluorinated urea/fused nitrogen heterocycle at 0.3246833344580741. The current observed increase accompanies substantially more unconventional N-fluorinated chemistry and cannot be read as improved synthetic quality.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest reports a stereocentre-notation rate of 0.0. The cited aryl-substituted diazacycles, complex ring junctions and multiply fluorinated sulfur rings contain centres requiring stereochemical definition; the cited unsaturated side chains also leave geometric configurations unspecified.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemical identity for the substituted saturated and unsaturated frameworks it produces.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Carry valid stereochemical identity through molecular construction and editing, and expose chemically distinct stereoisomers to task-local feedback. The present observations establish missing specification, not a demonstrated score benefit from adding it.

transferable_gaps.evidence: High-scoring digest molecules include amino-substituted alkynes with N–O attachments, carbonyl heterocycles with consecutive nonaromatic nitrogen atoms, and covalent N–F groups on nitrogen heterocycles. Familiar aromatic and amine scaffolds coexist with these motifs; ring availability is not the limitation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve chemically conventional functional-group environments when constructing heteroatom-rich molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent complete functional-group environments during de novo edits and retain access to ordinary amine, amide, ether and carbon-bound-halogen alternatives. Use the available unlabeled molecular chemistry and local feedback without assuming that chemically questionable high-scoring structures are already satisfactory endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A moderately sized aryl urea scores 0.48211544265448975 while an oversized polyene/polyring amide scores 2.6967182149798692e-39. A compact fluorinated heterocycle assembly scores 0.6427992966407532 while a much larger polyhydroxylated assembly scores 0.0. Elsewhere, dense ring fusion and repeated amide units do not exceed the more coherent parent arrangement.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently combines favorable ring and polar features within a restrained molecular size and topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support contractions and scaffold rearrangements that retain favorable local ring/polar relationships. Let each fresh search learn an appropriate size and topology from its own observations; a universal preference for smaller molecules is not established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The bounded best sets repeatedly vary hydroxylated aryl ureas, alkoxyamino azaaryl linkers, diaryl cyclic polyamines, nitrogen-rich carbonyl polycycles or fluorinated polyene/sulfonamides. Numerous constitutional changes preserve the same unusual attachment chemistry, while other scaffold families appear mainly in different seeds or at lower scores.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent alternatives are limited around the best observed architectures despite varied chemistry across the full trajectories.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Generate distinct ring and linker arrangements that preserve the favorable local chemical features learned from accepted observations. Treat scaffold diversity and small substituent variation as different capabilities, with chemically conventional alternatives remaining available for exploration.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
